mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the octet rule is a common misconception?

options.A: Atoms always achieve an octet by gaining or losing electrons.
options.C: Transition metals always obey the octet rule.
options.D: Noble gases have a complete octet.

mcqs.answer: Transition metals always obey the octet rule.
mcqs.explanation: Transition metals often have d‑orbitals that can accommodate more than eight electrons, so they do not always follow the octet rule. Options A, B and D are correct statements, whereas C is a misconception.

mcqs.question: Why is the Lewis symbol for chlorine written as •Cl with seven dots around the symbol?

options.B: Chlorine needs one more electron to complete an octet.
options.C: Chlorine shares one electron in a covalent bond.

mcqs.explanation: The number of dots in a Lewis symbol equals the number of valence electrons. Chlorine, being in group 17, possesses seven valence electrons, which are shown as seven dots. Option B describes the tendency to gain an electron, not the symbol itself. Options C and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly compares the Lewis structures of CO₂ and CO₃²⁻ in terms of octet satisfaction and resonance?

options.A: Both molecules have all atoms with an octet; CO₂ has two double bonds, while CO₃²⁻ has one double bond and two single bonds that are resonance‑averaged.
options.B: CO₂ satisfies the octet rule, but the central carbon in CO₃²⁻ has an incomplete octet.
options.C: CO₂ exhibits resonance structures, whereas CO₃²⁻ does not.
options.D: Both molecules have a central atom with an expanded octet.

mcqs.answer: Both molecules have all atoms with an octet; CO₂ has two double bonds, while CO₃²⁻ has one double bond and two single bonds that are resonance‑averaged.
mcqs.explanation: In CO₂, carbon forms two double bonds, giving carbon and each oxygen an octet. In the carbonate ion, carbon is bonded to three oxygens; one C=O double bond and two C–O single bonds are delocalised through resonance, so every atom still attains an octet. Options B, C and D contain incorrect statements about octet satisfaction or resonance.

mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds most clearly demonstrates a limitation of the octet rule?
mcqs.explanation: Boron in BF₃ has only six electrons around it after forming three covalent bonds, showing that elements in period 2 can be stable with an incomplete octet. CH₄, H₂O, and NH₃ all obey the octet rule, so they do not illustrate its limitation. This type of question frequently appears in competitive exams.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly states the octet rule?

options.A: Atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons so that each atom attains eight electrons in its valence shell.
options.B: Atoms always have eight protons in their nucleus.
options.C: Atoms share all of their electrons equally with neighboring atoms.
options.D: Only noble gases possess eight electrons in their outermost shell.

mcqs.answer: Atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons so that each atom attains eight electrons in its valence shell.
mcqs.explanation: The octet rule describes the tendency of atoms to achieve a stable configuration of eight valence electrons through electron transfer or sharing. Options B, C and D misrepresent the rule.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct Lewis symbol for an oxygen atom?
mcqs.explanation: Oxygen belongs to group 16 and has six valence electrons, which are represented by six dots surrounding the symbol O. Option B shows only two electrons, C shows an impossible eight for a neutral O atom, and D omits the valence electrons.

mcqs.question: Which description correctly distinguishes the Lewis structures of methane (CH₄) and ammonia (NH₃)?

options.A: CH₄ has four single C–H bonds and no lone pairs; NH₃ has three single N–H bonds and one lone pair on nitrogen.
options.B: CH₄ has three bonds and one lone pair; NH₃ has four bonds and no lone pairs.
options.C: Both molecules have the same number of bonds and lone pairs.
options.D: CH₄ contains a double bond, whereas NH₃ contains only single bonds.

mcqs.answer: CH₄ has four single C–H bonds and no lone pairs; NH₃ has three single N–H bonds and one lone pair on nitrogen.
mcqs.explanation: In methane, carbon forms four equivalent single bonds with hydrogen, fulfilling the octet with no lone pairs. In ammonia, nitrogen forms three single bonds with hydrogen and retains one lone pair, also satisfying the octet. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect bonding patterns.

mcqs.question: Which compound best illustrates a limitation of the octet rule due to an expanded octet?
mcqs.explanation: Sulfur in SF₆ uses its 3d orbitals to accommodate twelve valence electrons, exceeding the octet. H₂O, CO₂, and NH₃ all obey the octet rule, so they do not demonstrate this limitation.
